applicability.rationale: All required behavior is deterministic script/CLI accounting logic (identity threading, dedup keying, atomic file writes, JSON aggregation) with no model-authored output in the loop; one case carries an additional safety_sensitive risk for the never-gates/never-captures-disallowed-content guarantee.
Ticket isolation across runs is pure aggregation logic over persisted JSON files.

cases.given: Two factory runs recorded under external_ref gh-35 (one provider_exited_nonzero) and one run recorded under a different external_ref
cases.then: both gh-35 runs appear in contributing_runs and their usage.role totals are summed; the other ticket's run contributes nothing
cases.forbidden: Mixing another ticket's usage into gh-35's totals, or omitting the failed run from contributing_runs
counterexamples: Report includes tokens from a run recorded under a different external_ref

applicability.rationale: Dedup keys on (run_id, invocation_id); verifiable by direct assertion on repeated regeneration.

cases.given: A run's summary.json is regenerated twice (idempotent summary re-run) for the same run_id
cases.when: the ticket report is regenerated after each summary call
cases.then: the reported totals are identical both times; no observation is counted twice
cases.forbidden: Any increase in reported usage caused solely by re-running summary or the report itself
counterexamples: Second report shows double the tokens of the first with no new provider activity

applicability.rationale: usage_scope separation is a fixed field read on each observation record.

cases.given: One run contains both an orchestrator-scoped and a role-scoped observation event
cases.then: both subtotals appear separately under usage.role and usage.orchestrator, each with the correct values
cases.forbidden: Merging orchestrator-scoped and role-scoped usage into one number, or dropping either scope
counterexamples: usage.orchestrator and usage.role report the same combined total instead of their own scoped values

applicability.rationale: No cost adapter exists in this delivery; the field is a fixed constant in every code path.

cases.given: Any ticket with recorded runs, under this delivery's unchanged provider adapters
cases.then: cost.cost_status is always unknown and every *_usd field is null
cases.forbidden: Reporting any nonzero or zero dollar figure derived from token counts without a versioned pricing_source
counterexamples: cost.estimated_usd is a computed nonzero number with no pricing_source recorded

applicability.rationale: Observed-vs-not-observed is a fixed boolean derived from whether any orchestrator-scoped observation exists.

cases.given: A run with only a role-scoped observation (today's common case; the factory's own direct-provider call records no usage)
cases.then: usage.orchestrator.observed is false and usage.orchestrator.complete is false
cases.forbidden: Reporting usage.orchestrator as a complete zero total when no orchestrator-scoped observation was ever recorded
counterexamples: usage.orchestrator.input_tokens is 0 with complete:true despite no orchestrator observation existing

applicability.rationale: Reconstruction from events/ reuses the existing, already-tested _read_events dedup logic.

cases.given: A run whose events/ directory has recorded observations but whose process crashed before any summary call (no summary.json written)
cases.when: a fresh nightshift-ticket-report.py process runs after restart
cases.then: the interrupted run's already-recorded usage appears in the report via replayed_from_events
cases.forbidden: Silently dropping an interrupted run's already-recorded usage because summary.json is missing
counterexamples: contributing_runs omits the interrupted run entirely instead of marking it replayed_from_events

applicability.rationale: Breakdown and totals are computed from one pass over the same deduplicated observation list.

cases.given: Observations across two distinct stage/provider/model combinations for one ticket
cases.then: breakdown.by_stage, by_provider, and by_model each sum to the same totals as usage.role/usage.orchestrator
cases.forbidden: A breakdown whose sum disagrees with the reported overall total
counterexamples: by_stage sums to 900 tokens while usage.role reports 1000

applicability.rationale: Read-error handling on one run directory is a fixed try/except path with an explicit status field.

cases.given: One run's directory is made unreadable while a sibling run for the same ticket remains intact
cases.then: the process exits 0, the sibling run's usage is reported, and the unreadable run is marked read_error
cases.forbidden: A nonzero exit code, an uncaught exception, or silent omission of the sibling run's usage because of the other run's read failure
counterexamples: The whole report call exits nonzero because one run directory could not be read

applicability.rationale: Accounting must never gate engineering outcomes and must never capture disallowed content (prompts, transcripts, credentials); this is safety-sensitive because a defect here could silently block real engineering work or leak sensitive data through a metrics side channel, even though the implementation itself is ordinary deterministic code.

cases.given: Any accounting I/O or validation failure (unreadable run, malformed event, missing ticket index) during ticket report generation or observation recording
cases.when: the underlying role dispatch, factory run, or behavioral-proof gate proceeds independently
cases.then: the gate/dispatch outcome is unaffected by the accounting failure, and no prompt, transcript, file path, full command, or credential value is ever written to any metrics file
cases.forbidden: An accounting failure changing a gate/dispatch status, or any disallowed content type appearing in a metrics or ticket-index file
counterexamples: nightshift-agent.sh exits nonzero because the metrics event write failed
A ticket index file contains a raw prompt or an API key value
